SMTO-LLM-0064 — SMTO couldn't use the network port set for this model server

GUID: b80e4faa-22cd-545c-a320-a4ecb9d9b9c5
Slug: local-ai-port-in-use
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • Another program may already be using that port, or the address can't be used on that computer. SMTO didn't stop anything and didn't start the model server.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI runtimes on that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, to see whether this model server is already running. If an earlier start is still running, you can use it instead of starting another.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the Local AI Runtime profile, change port to another number such as 8001, and select Save. A different port avoids whatever program is already using the current one.
  3. Make sure host is 127.0.0.1 or an address that really belongs to that computer. The server can't listen on an address the computer doesn't have.
  4. Start the model server again in a new message that names the profile with @ (use Copy reference in Parameter Store). A task keeps the profile it started with, so only a new message picks up your saved changes.

What success looks like

  • The model server starts on the new port and its status shows ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't stop programs on that computer that SMTO didn't start. Another program using the port may belong to someone else.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A test bind to the profile's host and port on the Gateway failed (port already in use, an address that isn't on this host, or no permission for that port); no conflicting process was stopped and no model server was started.

What this means

  • A test bind to the requested host and port failed; occupation, an unavailable address or host permissions can produce the same socket error. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • A test bind to the requested host and port failed; occupation, an unavailable address or host permissions can produce the same socket error.

How to diagnose it

  • Have the Gateway operator inspect the exact bind address, listener ownership and socket error; a free port does not make an unavailable address valid.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, see what holds the port (for example ss -ltnp) and whether the profile's host IP belongs to this machine. Choose a free port, or correct host, in the Local AI Runtime Parameter and start a new task; never stop a process solely because it uses that port.
  • Correct the bind address or choose an available port in the accepted profile; do not stop a process solely because it uses that port.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended host/port can be bound without interfering with another service.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
